question.problem:
Find the coefficient of $(x-1)^{2}$ in the second-degree Taylor polynomial of $f(x)=\frac{1}{x+2}$ at $x=1.$ Do not round the answer.

The coefficient of $(x-1)^{2}$ is
{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
The second-degree Taylor polynomial of $f(x)$ about $x=1$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{2}(x) & =f(1)+{f}^{′}(1)(x-1)+\frac{{f}^{″}(1)}{2}(x-1)^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

The coefficient of $(x-1)^{2}$ in the above Taylor polynomial is

$$
\frac{{f}^{″}(1)}{2}.
$$

To find this coefficient, we start by computing the second derivative ${f}^{″}(x):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{1}{x+2}=(x+2)^{-1} \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =-(x+2)^{-2} \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =2(x+2)^{-3}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate ${f}^{″}(x)$ at $x=1.$ This gives

$$
{f}^{″}(1)=2(1+2)^{-3}=\frac{2}{27}.
$$

Finally, we determine the coefficient of $(x-1)^{2},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{f}^{″}(1)}{2}=\frac{(\frac{2}{27})}{2}=\frac{1}{27}\end{aligned}
$$
